text:
anya: Noticed elevated mTLS failures from eu->us region during the midnight canary. Failure window ~00:02-00:10 UTC, peaked ~2.8% handshakes. Opening thread so we can triage quickly.

ben: Logs show cert fetch failures and KMS denies around the same time. Snippet from proxy: 
```json
{"level":"warn","msg":"mtls: cert fetch failed","proxy":"ingress-eu-3","err":"keystore: decrypt failed (AccessDenied)"}
```
I captured KMS requestIds: req-34f7, req-34f8, req-3500.

leo: I deployed an RBAC cleanup earlier to remove stale subjects from `keystore-readers-eu` (PR 4892). Looking at git history the subject `ci-runner@infra` was removed at 23:58 UTC. Could be related.

nina: If that's the case it's an accidental permission removal. Suggest a short mitigation: rebind the subject, then trigger keystore reload and proxy KV eviction.

keystore-bot: policy-audit: detected modification to ClusterRoleBinding `keystore-readers-eu` by leo at 2026-03-22T23:58:02Z. No `rbac/approved` label found.

anya: Mitigation plan (fast):
- Patch: re-add `ci-runner@infra` to `keystore-readers-eu` (temp).
- Trigger keystore rolling restart for eu keystore replicas (graceful) to refresh credentials.
- Hit internal endpoint to flush proxy cert cache: POST /internal/keystore/flush?scope=proxy-cert
- If KMS denies persist after rebind, create an emergency allow grant and capture grant id for audit.
- Open an incident and page oncall if handshake error >1% for 15m.

ben: Creating temporary grant now (GCP pattern since key in gcp-kms):
```bash
# gcloud sample
gcloud kms keys add-iam-policy-binding keystore-eu --member=serviceAccount:ci-runner@infra.iam.gserviceaccount.com --role=roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyDecrypter --condition=None
```
I'll post the IAM binding id once applied and tail KMS audit logs.

leo: Re-added subject and rolled keystore pods. Also applied `kubectl annotate` to PR 4892 with `rbac/rollback=true` so we can track.

nina: Flushed proxy cache on eu proxies. Monitoring shows errors dropping to ~0.15% after 6 minutes.

anya: Good. Two follow-ups: 1) Add a pre-merge check that flags changes touching `keystore-` bindings and requires a security approver. 2) Ensure KMS audit logs for keystore keys are exported to long-term bucket (90 days) and indexed.

ben: Filed incident: INC-2026-1023, and created follow-up tasks in the ticket: RBAC guardrail, audit export, alert on KMS AccessDenied spike.

leo: Apologies for the noisy change; will include `rbac/approved` flow in next PR.

anya: Closing quick triage. We'll keep incident open for postmortem and remediation. Thanks team.
